summary: Extends the MRT export format for BGP routing data so it can record multiple paths for the same destination, as allowed by the BGP additional paths extension.

eli5.summary: A log of routes used to record only one way to reach a place. This lets the log note several ways, as BGP now allows.

questions: how to record multiple bgp paths in mrt
how does mrt record bgp add-paths
what is the mrt path identifier field
subtitle: New MRT record subtypes so routing archives can store several BGP paths for the same prefix.

tldr.problem: BGP can advertise multiple paths for one prefix, but the MRT archive format had no way to record the extra Path Identifier those advertisements carry.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds four BGP4MP/BGP4MP_ET subtypes and five TABLE_DUMP_V2 subtypes with an ADDPATH suffix, and adds a Path Identifier field to the RIB entries of the four AFI/SAFI-specific RIB subtypes.
tldr.outcome: A stateless MRT parser can tell from the subtype alone that additional-path encoding is in use. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and the extension is optional.

today: RFC 8050 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2017. It has not been obsoleted or updated, and it relies on RFC 6396 and RFC 7911.

sections.title: What This Extension Adds
sections.content:
The MRT record format from RFC 6396 gives researchers and engineers a way to encapsulate, export and archive routing protocol transactions and RIB snapshots. RFC 7911 defines a BGP extension that lets a speaker advertise multiple paths for the same address prefix without the new paths implicitly replacing earlier ones.

RFC 8050 is an optional extension to MRT. It introduces new subtype definitions so that multiple path advertisements can be represented in MRT files.
sections.eli5: A log of routes could only note one way to reach a place. This RFC lets the log hold several ways, as the newer BGP allows.

sections.title: Why New Subtypes Are Needed
sections.content:
MRT parsers are usually stateless. They do not watch the BGP session setup, so they cannot know which capabilities were negotiated. The additional paths extension changes how the BGP Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) is encoded for withdrawals and announcements. The parser has to be told how to read the NLRI, and the MRT subtype is the place to say it.

The same problem exists for RIB records. In RFC 6396 the prefix length and prefix fields are encoded the same way as the BGP NLRI encoding, so supporting the Path Identifier from RFC 7911 also needs new subtypes.
sections.eli5: A reader of the log cannot ask the people who wrote it what they meant. So the page type itself has to say how to read the entries.

sections.title: New BGP4MP and BGP4MP_ET Subtypes
sections.content:
Four new subtypes are defined for the BGP4MP and BGP4MP_ET types: BGP4MP_MESSAGE_ADDPATH, BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4_ADDPATH, BGP4MP_MESSAGE_LOCAL_ADDPATH and BGP4MP_MESSAGE_AS4_LOCAL_ADDPATH.

Their fields are identical to the equivalent non-additional-path versions in Section 4.4 of RFC 6396. They continue to encapsulate the entire BGP message in the BGP message field. Only the subtype tells the parser that the NLRI inside uses additional-path encoding.
sections.eli5: The pages look the same as before. Only the page title changes, to warn the reader that the entries inside carry extra labels.

sections.title: New TABLE_DUMP_V2 Subtypes and the Path Identifier
sections.content:
Five new subtypes are defined for TABLE_DUMP_V2: RIB_IPV4_UNICAST_ADDPATH, RIB_IPV4_MULTICAST_ADDPATH, RIB_IPV6_UNICAST_ADDPATH, RIB_IPV6_MULTICAST_ADDPATH and RIB_GENERIC_ADDPATH. Their fields are identical to the non-additional-path versions in Section 4.3 of RFC 6396, except for the RIB Entries field of the four AFI/SAFI-specific subtypes.

To keep the record compaction of the common subtypes, and to let several RIB Entries sit in one record, the RIB Entries field is redefined. Each entry gains a Path Identifier field, placed after the Originated Time and before the Attribute Length.

RIB_GENERIC_ADDPATH is different. Its fields match Section 4.3.3 of RFC 6396 and carry the raw, additional-path-enabled AFI/SAFI/NLRI, and its RIB Entries are not redefined.
sections.eli5: Each saved route entry gets a small extra label saying which of the several roads it is. The catch-all page type needs no change.

sections.title: Assigned Subtype Codes
sections.content: IANA assigned the codes in the Multi-threaded Routing Toolkit (MRT) registry. The four BGP4MP subtypes take values 8 to 11 in both the BGP4MP and BGP4MP_ET registries. The five TABLE_DUMP_V2 subtypes take values 8 to 12.
sections.eli5: Each new page type was given its own number so everyone uses the same name for it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC does not believe it adds new security considerations, but the considerations of RFC 6396 apply equally, because the extension permits export of more detailed routing data.

An organization that stores its BGP routing information in MRT should know that these extensions allow more detailed network path information to be stored. An organization that peers with public BGP collectors and enables additional paths on a session is exporting not only its best paths but potentially other paths within its networks, and should weigh the implications.
sections.eli5: Writing down every road you know, not only your favorite, tells outsiders more about your town. Think before you share the longer list.
